result:
Both test classes compiled successfully on the first attempt (`compiled OK`), producing `out/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReaderAgentTest.class` and `JsonWriterAgentTest.class`.

Summary of what was written:

- **`tests/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReaderAgentTest.java`** — ~48 JUnit 3.8 (`junit.framework.TestCase`) test methods covering: empty/nested array & object traversal, `peek()` non-consumption, the documented Number Handling coercions (`nextString`/`nextInt`/`nextLong`/`nextDouble` reading across string↔number tokens), every documented `IllegalStateException`/`IOException`/`NumberFormatException` case (wrong token type, closed reader, non-exact int/long, non-finite double), structural mismatches (`beginArray` on an object, `endArray` before exhausted, etc.), the full strict-vs-lenient bullet list from `setLenient`'s javadoc (non-execute prefix, top-level scalars, unquoted strings, comments, stray/semicolon separators, `=` separators), `skipValue()`, and `getPath()`.
- **`tests/com/google/gson/stream/JsonWriterAgentTest.java`** — ~34 tests covering structural encoding, fluent `this`-returning chain, string escaping/null handling, boolean/long/double/Number encoding, strict rejection of NaN/Infinity (`IllegalArgumentException`), `name(null)` (`NPE`), `jsonValue` raw passthrough, `setIndent` pretty-printing vs compact, lenient vs strict top-level values, the class-level "malformed calls throw `IllegalStateException`" contract, `close()` on an incomplete document throwing `IOException`, flush/close delegation to the underlying `Writer` (via a small self-contained `CountingWriter` helper), HTML-safe escaping, and `serializeNulls` semantics.

Since `JsonToken` isn't included anywhere in `api/` (only `JsonReader`/`JsonWriter` are documented), I relied only on the one enum reference the javadoc itself makes (`JsonToken.NULL` in the example code) plus `JsonToken.NUMBER`, which are the two constants exercised in the reader tests.
